clue.text: A bit of chicken curry

definitions.meaning: the fleshy red crest on a cockerel's head is part of the bird
to curry a horse is to groom it with a toothed tool

explanation.definitionFit: A cock's crest is a comb, and grooming a horse with a currycomb is to comb it.

clue.text: Think deeply about cottage I renovated

indicators.note: renovated means done up and rebuilt, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Musing on a little house one has done up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or mull something over at length is to cogitate on it.

clue.text: Fellow admiral once credited with magical powers

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Sir Francis Drake was an Elizabethan admiral

explanation.surface: A man, a former admiral, was thought to have magic powers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the forked root of this plant was long believed to be magical.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked root of this plant was long believed to have occult and medicinal powers.

clue.text: Bad oarsman can be a successful fisherman

definitions.meaning: a rower who jams the blade in the water and is jolted is said to do this
taken literally, an angler who lands a crustacean

explanation.surface: A clumsy rower turns out to be good at landing fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, catching a crab means fouling the stroke so the oar handle jerks back at the rower; read literally, it is a good day's fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowing idiom for a botched stroke reads literally as netting a shellfish, the mark of a lucky angler.

clue.text: Land shaped like a circle or a ring

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell slowly

explanation.surface: A piece of ground in the shape of a hoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like part of the shape description but is a verb, as of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A coral island encircling a lagoon is a ring-shaped piece of land.

clue.text: Riddle sister posed after company party

indicators.note: posed after says the sister is placed following the company

parts.note: a sister is a nun
a drum is an old word for a large evening party

explanation.surface: A nun sets a puzzle after a firm's party.
explanation.walkthrough: A drum was an eighteenth-century word for a crowded social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or question with a hidden or punning answer.

clue.text: Increasing power of daring gang is awful

indicators.note: awful means terrible, so the letters are badly mangled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bold gang's growing strength is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrandise is to enlarge the power, rank or wealth of someone.

clue.text: Work out in grounds

definitions.meaning: grounds are the justification or cause for something

explanation.definitionFit: To think logically is to work things out, and a justification is the grounds for an action.

clue.text: Mate has to earn the specified amount

parts.note: bud is slang for a friend, a mate
to get money is to earn it

explanation.surface: A friend must earn exactly the sum set out.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget is the amount allotted for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Left inside, being on edge

indicators.note: inside says the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone who departed while feeling nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has left a place has departed; the past participle of go.

clue.text: Start watch — hunter, perhaps, with protective cover

parts.note: a hunter is a horse bred for hunting, an example of a mount
a guard is a shield or shielding cover, as on a machine

explanation.surface: A sentry begins duty, with a huntsman and a shield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hunter, perhaps' suggests a person, but it is the horse a rider sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on sentry duty is the idiom for beginning a spell of watch-keeping.

clue.text: Inspects only 50%, we hear, being drunk

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is spoken and a same-sounding one is entered

parts.note: inspects is sees over, only 50% is half, giving half sees over

explanation.surface: A half-hearted inspector checks only half of things, apparently while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: HALF SEES OVER said aloud matches an old phrase for tipsy. The held clue's '0% is an OCR misreading of 50%.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for being well on the way to intoxication, likened to a ship halfway across.

clue.text: Man boards moving train in waterproof hat

indicators.note: boards means gets aboard, so the man goes inside the vehicle's letters
moving says the letters of train are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: Paul is a man's name

explanation.surface: A fellow gets on a departing train wearing a rain hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a generic person, but a man's first name is wanted; the surface train is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a tarred canvas sheet, the word names a sailor's tarred or oilskin hat worn against spray.

clue.text: A flower came up

parts.note: the rose is a familiar garden bloom

explanation.surface: A bloom pushed up out of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up is to rise, and this is its past tense.

clue.text: Have on (the pillion?)

definitions.meaning: to have someone on is to deceive or tease them
a pillion is a passenger seat behind a motorcyclist, so giving someone a lift there

explanation.surface: A joke about tricking someone, or carrying them on the back seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed second definition is the literal sense: carrying someone behind you on a motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deceive or con, and literally means giving someone a lift.

clue.text: Tries to disrupt actual trial

indicators.note: to disrupt means to break into, so the tries word splits the actual word

parts.note: actual means real
a judge hears a case when trying it

explanation.surface: Attempts to wreck an actual test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts, but in court a judge tries, or hears, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice run before a performance is a trial of it.

clue.text: Amusement — girl conceals it

indicators.note: conceals says one piece hides the other within it

parts.note: Hilary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl hides her amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Merriment or loud laughter is amusement.

clue.text: Abandon plane? It's acceptable

parts.note: a jet is a plane
'tis is an old contraction of it is
on means acceptable, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: Should we abandon the aircraft? That is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' seems part of the definition, but it gives JET.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw overboard or discard is to abandon.

clue.text: Concord rules in this up-to-date county

parts.note: something up to date is new
Hampshire is a county on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Agreement governs this modern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concord' reads as harmony, but it is the capital city of this US state; Hampshire is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Concord is the state capital, so it governs this New England state.

clue.text: Hell!, objectionable chap said, getting excited

indicators.note: said tells us the two words are spoken to give a matching sound

parts.note: heck is a mild word for hell, and tick is British slang for a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A man swears at an unpleasant fellow and grows agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: HECK TICK said aloud gives the answer; 'tick' as a nasty person is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic and feverish activity is a state of getting excited.

clue.text: Bird with magical powers?

explanation.definitionFit: A small falcon shares its name with King Arthur's wizard.

clue.text: Paradoxical odds?

parts.note: betting odds of one to one carry a name that is the opposite of odd, hence the paradox

explanation.definitionFit: Odds of one to one in betting go by a name meaning not odd, which is the paradox.

clue.text: Waiting on occupant, daughter moves in after a time

indicators.note: after says the remaining letters follow the a-and-time pair
moves in says the daughter takes up residence inside the occupant's letters

parts.note: a tenant occupies a rented property

explanation.surface: A tenant's daughter moves into the flat after some time, waiting on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who serves or accompanies another is said to be waiting on them; the adjective means accompanying or serving.

clue.text: Peg, involved in row, disrupted hotel

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clothes peg caught up in a quarrel that upset a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin set in the gunwale of a boat acts as the fulcrum for an oar.

clue.text: Entertainment — when it's live, one is diverted

indicators.note: diverted means turned aside from its course, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken with its letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Fun when a broadcast goes out live and someone is amused by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' also hints at entertainment, but here it rearranges ITS LIVE ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast programmes watched at home are a chief form of entertainment.

clue.text: Fail to meet young lady

definitions.meaning: The title for a girl or unmarried woman

explanation.definitionFit: Failing to catch someone is missing them, and a girl is addressed by this title.

clue.text: Under supervision, prisoner went fishing

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
to troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat

explanation.surface: A convict on supervised release went out angling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept under supervision is regulated or held in check.

clue.text: Song that man's heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: that man is him, with 's as is

explanation.surface: A tune that a fellow has heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise.
